newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P assigns BBB+ rating to Finnish Rauma.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns BBB+ rating to Finnish Rauma.

text.p: U.S. credit ratings agency Standard & Poor's on Thursday said it had assigned a long-term rating of BBB+ with a stable outlook to Finland's engineering group Rauma Oy.
It assigned the company a short-term corporate credit rating of A-2.
S&P said the ratings reflect the Rauma group's diverse earnings and cash flow base, its strong world market position in core businesses and sound financial profile and policies.
"Demand is cyclical but the swings are mitigated by Rauma's worldwide presence," S&P said in a statement.

"Rauma's sales are further fairly evenly spread over its four business groups, and although several of them have the forest products industry as their main customer -- around 60 percent of Rauma's sales -- the demand for Rauma's products nevertheless follows slightly different cycles."
S&P said the outlook for the company was stable.
"Rauma's diverse earnings and cash flow base and flexible cost base should help to mitigate the pressure on margins in cyclical downturns," the agency said.
"Nevertheless, to balance the operating risk, it is expected that Rauma will maintain a conservative financial profile."
Rauma on Thursday said it expected profitability for 1996 to be good as its released its January-August results.
Rauma posted a 671 million markka profit before extraordinary items in 1995. In January-August, the group's profit rose 16 percent from a year ago to 427 million markka.
